data.title: Spaced repetition may be a helpful tool to develop or change habits
data.contentMarkdown:
# Spaced repetition may be a helpful tool to develop or change habits

Imagine that you read an article which suggests something like this:

> Going around in circles with a challenging prioritization exercise? If none of the factors seems especially decisive on their own, you’re probably not going to get anywhere with a big pro/con table. You’ll need to either create new choices, identify more powerful axes of evaluation, or accept that you can’t make a strongly-informed choice.

You could memorize pieces of this with a [[z2D1qPwddPktBjpNuwYFVva:::Spaced repetition memory system]], but you can also use the same system to help “install” this habit in your mind. Here are some example questions you might try:

> Q: Recall a situation in which you went around in circles endlessly trying to prioritize various options. (Generate one you haven’t thought about before for this question)
> A: [blank]

> Q: Imagine an unusual series of concrete steps you might take next time you find yourself stuck in an unclear prioritization exercise. (Generate a series of steps that you haven’t generated before)
> A: [blank]

> Q: Imagine a specific situation in which you would have trouble escaping a prioritization quagmire by finding a single decisive factor. (Generate one you haven’t thought about before)
> A: [blank]

After you’ve answered this type of prompt about a specific habit a few times, it’s often helpful to make much more specific prompts to reinforce that habit. For example ([via Kanjun, 2020-07-01](https://twitter.com/kanjun/status/1278501271226298368)): “When I pick up my toothbrush in the morning…” “…get my phone and open Anki.”

This is an example of [[zB92WZZ5baBHKZPPbWMbYEv:::Spaced repetition systems can be used to program attention]].

---

## References

Conversation with [[Florent Crivello]], 2019-11-17

Related notion from [[zAgiS9VaDo969dpx9eDntgA:::Alexey Guzey]]: [Instilling Novel Thought Patterns and Making Your Long-Term Memory Accountable with Anki - Alexey Guzey](https://guzey.com/things/software/anki/#instilling-novel-thought-patterns-with-anki)

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Spaced repetition memory systems can be used to prompt application, synthesis, and creation
contextBlocks: [[z9AH3dD42uGiJzR1WH1eo7n:::Spaced repetition may be a helpful tool to develop or change habits]]

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Unusual applications of spaced repetition memory systems
contextBlocks: [[z9AH3dD42uGiJzR1WH1eo7n:::Spaced repetition may be a helpful tool to develop or change habits]]

You can imagine creating cards about new habits (“Think of a new concrete situation in which I’ll have trouble leaving space for others to speak.”) or values (“What’s an unusual recent situation in which you thought on the century scale?”); see [[z9AH3dD42uGiJzR1WH1eo7n:::Spaced repetition may be a helpful tool to develop or change habits]]. More exotic [[z9hscgkG2TeqgUtu3vAEW3U:::Spaced everything]] systems can be used to schedule arbitrary fine-grained tasks associated with some new identity, like iteratively reaching out to interesting people in a new field.

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Embedded prompt templates may actively scaffold prompt-writing for mnemonic medium readers
contextBlocks: [[zJSUEFHrJLVspreiCpnAnKJ:::The mnemonic medium may help scaffold prompt-writing through author-provided prompts]], but sometimes it’s particularly important that the reader write their own prompts—e.g. particularly when the impact is personal rather than intellectual, as in [[z9AH3dD42uGiJzR1WH1eo7n:::Spaced repetition may be a helpful tool to develop or change habits]]. In these situations, what if the author could help the reader write their own prompts? Perhaps they could provide a set of prompt templates to remix, interleaved directly into the reading experience as in this sketch:
Q. Why does Matt suggest that activities thought to be low-agency (repetition, memorization) are actually good for developing agency?
[[z9AH3dD42uGiJzR1WH1eo7n:::Spaced repetition may be a helpful tool to develop or change habits]]
